title: Raíces Cubanas
subtitle: A 90-minute dance-theatre show in two parts
lead: The sound of the waters echoes through the myths and legends that shape Cuban identity. The many cultural currents that coexist on the island come together to form the soul of its people. Rebellious, joyful, musical and united, these qualities reflect the true spirit of Cuba.
text: Raíces Cubanas, presented by the Generación Abbilona Association and its International Folkloric Company of Traditional Cuban Dances, brings this spirit to the stage. The performance is a journey through musical and dance traditions of African and Cuban origin, tracing the richness of Cuban culture from the colonial era to the present day.

parts.label: Part one
parts.title: Raíces
parts.text: The first part explores the Afro-Cuban religious and mythological world. It highlights the influence of the orishas and other African deities on Cuban culture, with choreographies dedicated to Elegguá, Ogún, Yemayá, Changó and Oyá, as well as a portrayal of the journey of enslaved Africans to Cuba. It shows how their spiritual beliefs and musical traditions became a fundamental part of Cuban identity.

parts.label: Part two
parts.title: La Cubanía
parts.text: The second part celebrates the popular music and dance genres born from the birth of the Cuban Republic up to the present day: danzón, mambo, cha-cha-chá, son, the street vendors' chants (pregones), rumba and the Cuban carnival. It highlights the racial and cultural blending that sets Cuba apart and celebrates the joy and diversity of the Cuban people.
